question: What are noise models?
answer: Noise models are components of a noisy‑channel system that simulate the kinds of mistakes humans make when producing text. In the described system each noise model is implemented as a weighted finite‑state transducer (wFST) that takes an error‑free sentence as input and, with a specified probability, outputs a version containing a particular type of error (e.g., spelling errors, article‑choice errors, preposition‑choice errors, insertion errors) [Source 1]. Multiple noise models can be combined (layered) to allow several error types to appear in the same sentence [Source 2]. Together with a base language model, the noise model forms the second main component of the overall noisy‑channel model [Source 4].
